title: Reading differently with ChatGPT: EFL learners’ use of Question-Answer Relationship strategy
extended_summary:
This qualitative study examines how university EFL learners’ reading comprehension developed when they used ChatGPT together with the Question-Answer Relationship (QAR) strategy. The paper is motivated by the need for more individualized reading support in EFL contexts, where learners often struggle with vocabulary, sentence complexity, synthesis across text, and inferencing. The authors ask how learners’ comprehension changes when ChatGPT is used not as a simple answer engine, but as a dialogic reading partner within a structured comprehension framework.

The intervention/approach consisted of five guided reading sessions over five weeks with GPT-4o mini, combined with QAR-based questioning and follow-up reflection. Participants first read TOEFL-style texts and answered comprehension questions, then created their own QAR-type questions, and then interacted with ChatGPT by generating, comparing, and refining questions and answers. The study used three rounds of semi-structured interviews with 35 first-year undergraduate students at a university in northern China; the analysis was thematic and focused on learners’ experiences across different QAR levels (Right There, Think and Search, Author and You).

Findings suggest a developmental progression in comprehension. At the most basic level, ChatGPT helped learners identify explicit information, vocabulary, and sentence-level meaning. As they moved to Think and Search questions, they began synthesizing across text segments, summarizing main ideas, and tracking logical relationships. At the highest level, Author and You questions supported inferencing, interpretation of tone and intent, and critical engagement with authorial choices. The study concludes that ChatGPT can support EFL reading when paired with explicit strategy instruction, but its value depends on learners’ critical use and awareness of limitations such as vague definitions, imperfect sentence parsing, overly literal summaries, and unreliable inferential explanations.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI chatbot based on GPT models, capable of generating, explaining, and adapting language in dialogue.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as a dialogic reading partner alongside the Question-Answer Relationship (QAR) strategy in guided EFL reading sessions; students asked it to generate questions, explain vocabulary and sentences, and support comprehension and inference.

findings.finding_summary: In a qualitative study with 35 first-year university EFL learners over five weeks, participants reported that ChatGPT helped them progress from locating explicit information to synthesizing across texts and making inferences. The paper reports developmental gains in reading comprehension strategies, but no effect sizes were reported.
findings.measure: Semi-structured interview reports of reading comprehension development using QAR categories (Right There, Think and Search, Author and You)

findings.finding_summary: Participants said ChatGPT supported vocabulary clarification, sentence breakdown, summarization, and interpretation of tone/author intent during reading. Learners also noted limitations such as vague definitions, unclear parsing of long sentences, copied text in summaries, and occasional inferential inaccuracies.
findings.measure: Semi-structured interview reports of reading support across vocabulary, syntax, summarization, and inferential reading

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative interview study with 35 participants, so it provides rich descriptive evidence but not causal or quantitative impact estimates. The methodology is transparent and systematic, but the evidence level is below experimental designs.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports meaningful positive experiences and strategy development, but it does not provide effect sizes or standardized outcome gains. The impact is therefore promising yet unclear in magnitude.
